title: Contain and bind late Network rerun state paths
summary: Treat Network rerun batch IDs as bounded opaque identifiers, resolve only the canonical direct-child state file, require any stored state path and persisted batch identity to match, and bind late writes to server-created reclaim job/worker/batch/row/source evidence.
reason: Remediate P2 AUDIT-FIND-W01-029. An authenticated late worker report could interpolate parent, absolute, or Windows-style path components into the rerun state path and rewrite any reachable schema-compatible batch file with a matching row key.
affected_areas: Network CSV rerun late and duplicate done reports
behavior_before: The late fallback concatenated the wire batch_id into root / '<batch_id>.json', trusted an unbounded batch_state_path when present, did not compare payload.batch_id, discarded rerun batch/row metadata during reclaim, and fell through to ordinary queue removal when rerun recording returned false.
behavior_after: Only 1-128 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen batch IDs are accepted. The resolved direct-child path must equal any stored batch_state_path and remain beneath the canonical Network root; payload.batch_id must match before mutation. Reclaim reports preserve and must match job, worker, job kind, batch, row, and normalized source. Any signed rerun conflict is durably diagnosed and returns 409 without batch or queue mutation.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py: Windows/POSIX parent, absolute, separator, extension, and mismatched stored-path matrix is rejected while the canonical opaque ID resolves.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py: a schema-valid file whose persisted batch_id differs is not written.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_rerun_claims.py: registry reclaim job, worker, and source mismatches cannot mutate late row evidence.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_inflight_registry.py: reclaim reports retain server-created Network rerun job kind, batch ID, and row key.
tests/python/desktop/test_network_security.py: HMAC-signed traversal and persisted-batch mismatch reports return 409, preserve batch bytes, and never remove ordinary queue state.

notes: High-risk state-path and authorization boundary. Current batch creation uses network-rerun-<16 hex> IDs and legacy active tests use batch-1, both inside the new grammar; no permissive legacy path migration is needed. No source media, media policy, destination policy, or publish behavior changes. Representative media is not required.
